# TouchScreenKeyboard

The platform's on-screen keyboard (Unity: TouchScreenKeyboard).

Availability: **PSX** no | **PSP** yes | **PS2** no

The component or type needs the `osk` feature (system on-screen keyboard). If it is missing: read the text from a UI field.

One keyboard at a time. The text lives in a fixed buffer of 64 characters; there is no heap.

## Members

| Member | PSX | PSP | PS2 | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `static bool Open(const char* initial, const char* title, u32 maxLen)` | no | yes | no | Opens it. False when unsupported or already open. |
| `static Status status()` | yes | yes | yes | `None`, `Visible`, `Done`, `Canceled`, `LostFocus` (the platform failed it). |
| `static const char* text()` | yes | yes | yes | The typed text; final once `status()` is `Done`. Never null. |

## Notes

- `status()` and `text()` compile everywhere and report `None` and an empty text where there is no keyboard; `Open` is gated.
- On the PSP the game keeps drawing while the keyboard is open, and the system draws it on top.

## Example

```cpp
if (!asked && TouchScreenKeyboard::Open("", "Your name")) asked = true;
if (TouchScreenKeyboard::status() == TouchScreenKeyboard::Status::Done) name = TouchScreenKeyboard::text();
```
